newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank of Canada Q1 earnings rise, stock soars.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank of Canada Q1 earnings rise, stock soars.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada, Canada's largest bank, reported increased first-quarter earnings on Wednesday that topped market expectations and sent its shares soaring in Toronto and New York.

The Toronto-based bank said its earnings for the first quarter ended Jan. 31 rose to C$399 million (US$291 million) or C$1.18 (86 cents) a share from C$356 million (US$259.8 million) or C$1.01 (74 cents) a share in the same period a year earlier.
Analysts had forecast earnings per share of C$1.15 (84 cents).
Royal Bank's shares skyrocketed C$2.05 to C$57.70 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday and by $1.25 to $42 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The bank said the earnings exceeded even its own forecasts and came despite a C$50 million (US$36.5 million) charge for its recent acquisition of Canadian brokerage Richardson Greenshields Ltd.

"Growth in revenues exceeded our targets as favourable economic and capital market conditions led to strong performances from the Wealth Management (mutual funds, brokerage, investment management) and lending operations," Royal Bank Chairman John Cleghorn said in a statement.
Cleghorn said further improvement in credit quality was evident in reductions in both impaired loans and the provision for credit losses.

Also on Wednesday, shareholders at Royal Bank's annual meeting in Vancouver easily defeated proposals by dissident shareholders to cap senior executive salaries and separate the offices of chief executive and chairman.
